scope: One independent science/task-fidelity review of all 10 frozen modern written questions, reusing the completed D006 source-only blind solutions.
source_binding: Actual template bytes match the supplied freeze. Embedded source.data equals the faithful source object; all 10 source_text values, source numbers, groups, page references and figure references match. Every original dollar-delimited formula/data span is retained and every numeric_changes list is empty. Modern lines reconstruct their corresponding text exactly.

question_reviews.reasoning: 100 g and cycle frequency 2 Hz are unchanged. Fixed support, negligible spring mass/resistance and Hooke's law make the free-SHM inference well posed: omega=2*pi*nu and k=m*omega^2=1.6*pi^2 N/m, approximately 15.8 N/m. The learner must still derive stiffness and convert units; no solution formula is supplied.

The historical name, cathedral setting and 98 m datum remain expressly attributed to the original book, without a current-device measurement claim. Point-bob, fixed-support, small-angle modeling and the support-to-center-of-mass length definition support T approximately 2*pi*sqrt(98 m/g). Requiring a stated g for a numerical estimate resolves the source's unspecified gravity convention; g=9.8 m/s^2 gives approximately 19.87 s. The period task remains, and this review independently validates no historical measurement.

Counts 10 and 6 over the same duration, the 16 cm length difference and the l1/l2 correspondence are retained. Common location and ideal small-angle motion justify T1/T2=6/10 and l1/l2=9/25; the first pendulum is shorter, giving l1=9 cm and l2=25 cm. Defining the difference as longer minus shorter does not disclose which label is longer or remove the two-length reasoning task.

The source mass ratio 1/81 and radius ratio 3.7 are unchanged and identified as approximate data. Same pendulum length, surface locations, spherical symmetry and negligible rotation/topographic effects support gM/gE=3.7^2/81 and TM/TE=9/3.7, approximately 2.43. The question retains the gravity-to-period derivation and increase/decrease judgment; it introduces no unconditional claim about a complete clock continuing to operate or retaining calibration.

Both zero initial velocities, simultaneous start, fixed support, light inextensible string, common uniform gravity and negligible interactions/resistance are explicit. Nonzero small-angle release starts the pendulum at a turning point; its first equilibrium crossing takes approximately (pi/2)*sqrt(l/g), whereas the dropped point ball falls l in sqrt(2*l/g). The falling ball arrives first. The original two-motion comparison remains open written reasoning, with an added request to explain its basis.

The 1 cm displacement, 5 Hz frequency, 2 s interval and negligible damping remain. Explicit rest release and timing from release establish amplitude 1 cm; fixed-support Hookean dynamics with negligible spring mass permit 10 full cycles and distance 10*4A=40 cm. The path-length definition correctly distinguishes distance from the zero net displacement; it supplies neither the per-cycle path nor the answer.

x=5*cos(2*pi*t), centimeters, seconds and displacement phase 5*pi/6 are unchanged. Identifying phase as the displacement cosine argument and requesting a signed projection resolves rather than changes the task. The retained derivative is vx=-10*pi*sin(2*pi*t) cm/s; velocity amplitude is positive 10*pi cm/s and the requested projection is -5*pi cm/s. Both amplitude extraction and signed phase evaluation remain required.

200 g, 16 N/m and 2 cm are retained, as are all three requested quantities. Fixed-end Hookean motion, negligible spring mass/friction/air resistance and explicit potential-energy zeros justify omega=sqrt(80) rad/s, E=0.0032 J and speed amplitude approximately 0.1789 m/s. Gravity/support do no work on the stated horizontal motion. Defining energy and speed amplitude removes additive-energy/sign ambiguity without supplying the solution or dropping the energy task.

The small square wooden block, frictionless spherical bowl, curvature radius R and fig-23 reference are retained. Negligible block size, point modeling, ignored rotation, maintained contact and a vertical section through the lowest point justify using the bowl radius R for the idealized point path rather than an exact finite-block center-of-mass radius. Explicit small central angle and an approximate-period request support theta''+(g/R)*theta approximately 0 and T approximately 2*pi*sqrt(R/g). This resolves the blind solution's amplitude/path-model ambiguities; no rolling correction or exact arbitrary-amplitude law is introduced.

Approximately 8 m spacing and the 1.5 s free period are retained. Uniform speed, similar bumps, a small-amplitude weakly damped single linear mode and explicit omission of higher harmonics define the intended model. Comparing passage frequency v/d with approximately 1/T0 gives v approximately 5.33 m/s, or 19.2 km/h. Wording requests approximate near-resonant pronounced motion, not an exact real-vehicle maximum; it still requires constructing and explaining the frequency comparison.

boundaries: All 10 original tasks remain in order with their requested outputs; cross-page exercise 6 retains p0046#14 -> p0047#1 and exercise 10 retains p0047#6 + p0047#8. Clarifying assumptions/definitions do not substitute answers or remove the spring, pendulum, free-fall, signed-phase, energy, constrained-sliding or resonance topics.
